site.name: ccam
site.title: ccam: Claude Code Account Manager and account switcher
site.description: ccam (Claude Code Account Manager) is a free, open-source tool to use several Claude Code accounts on one computer and switch between them with one command.

facts.what: ccam is a free, open-source command-line tool that lets you use several Claude Code accounts on one computer and switch between them with one command.
facts.how: Each account keeps its own login in a separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, while MCP servers, settings, CLAUDE.md, extensions and conversation history can be shared between accounts, so you can continue a conversation on another account when one reaches its usage limit.
facts.install: Install it on Linux, macOS or Windows with one command, then run ccam add for each account.
facts.official: ccam is an unofficial project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.

landing.headline: Several Claude Code accounts. One terminal.
landing.lede: Add each account once. Switch with ccam work or a shortcut such as ccwork. When one account hits its limit, carry on in the next with the same conversation.
landing.thenAdd: Then add your first account with {command}.
landing.boardLabel: Example session: when one account hits its limit, ccam continues the conversation on another

demo.title: When an account hits its limit

steps.body: Start Claude Code as one of your accounts with its shortcut.
That account reaches its 5-hour limit, and Claude Code stops.
See the 5-hour and weekly usage of every account at once.
Open the account with the most room and pick up the same conversation.

flow.body: Creates a separate config folder for the account, opens the Claude login in your browser and, if you want one, gives the account a shortcut you name yourself, such as ccwork.
Starts Claude Code as that account. Everything after the name goes to Claude Code unchanged, and ccam adds about 4 milliseconds before it starts.
Chooses what the accounts in a group share with each other. MCP servers, settings, CLAUDE.md and extensions are shared from the start; logins never are.
Shows the 5-hour and weekly usage of every account at once, so you know which one has room left.
Opens the same conversation in the next account when the current one reaches its limit.
Checks links, permissions and logins, and repairs what it safely can. Every change to your files keeps a backup.

commands.ccam: Open the dashboard: accounts, agents, groups, folders, extensions and health
commands.name: Start Claude Code as that account; arguments are passed through unchanged
commands.fallback: For -p runs: at a usage limit, run the same command again as the account with the most room
commands.add: Add an account: config folder, login and an optional shortcut
commands.next: Open the next account; --continue carries the conversation over, --auto picks the most room
commands.usage: Show 5-hour and weekly usage of every account
commands.share: Show what an account shares, and through which group
commands.group: Create and change groups: what a set of accounts share, moved with a plan

commands.logout: Log an account out: its login and its MCP server sign-ins
commands.rename: Rename an account; its shortcut keeps its name
commands.remove: Remove an account: it is logged out, and its folder goes to the trash folder
commands.import: Register an existing ~/.claude folder in place
commands.doctor: Check links, permissions, logins and versions, and repair
commands.statusline: Show the account and usage in Claude Code's status line
commands.shims: Recreate the shortcut links of all accounts
commands.shortcut: Show, create, rename or remove an account's shortcut command, such as ccwork
commands.folder: Use an account in a folder and below when no account is named
commands.pick: Print the account with the most room, for scripts and parallel workers
commands.ext: Show the skills, commands, plugins, MCP servers and hooks each account loads
commands.agents: List the background agents and open sessions of every account
commands.attach: Open a background session as the account that started it
commands.ccusage: Show ccusage's token and cost reports for the conversations of every account
commands.hook: Run by the ccam plugin's hooks in Claude Code (usage limits, /ccam:switch)
commands.update: Update ccam to the latest release after checking its checksum
commands.completion: Print bash, zsh or PowerShell completion
